messages:
Maya Chen: heads up — we just got an escalation from a hosted customer (acct: acme-inc) reporting p99 latency ~2x higher starting ~04:10 UTC. Dashboards show p95 unchanged but p99 jumped from ~320ms -> ~760ms on rtx-a100 pool for short-sequence traffic (typical seq ~32-64). :eyes:
Ben Park: did anything land to runtime or kernels overnight? I can check deploy history but any known perf changes?
Maya Chen: deploy-bot shows a canary at 03:45 UTC, commit abc123 — "kernel-selection: prefer flashattn2 for supported devices" (PR #3421).
deploy-bot: canary rollout completed (canary: 10% traffic) — buildkite/job/98765 — commit abc123 — status: succeeded :white_check_mark:
Olivia Reyes: I can repro locally against canary image. Using our loadtest client with seq=64 + batch=1 I see median ~270ms but p99 ~740ms. With the older image (abc122) p99 ~310ms. Repro steps below:
```
# quick repro
python tools/load_client.py --model gpt-small --seq 64 --batch 1 --repeat 1000 --endpoint https://canary-api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# or curl
curl -X POST https://canary-api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello" , "max_tokens":64 }'
```
Results: p50 260ms, p95 330ms, p99 740ms (canary). Old: p99 310ms.
Samir Patel: interesting — sequence lengths are short. FlashAttention should help long seqs but we've seen FlashAttn overhead for tiny seq because kernel selection/tiling overhead dominates. Anything in the selector logic changed?
Olivia Reyes: yes PR changed kernel priority order: flashattn2 jumped ahead of sdpa for all supported GPUs. The selector no longer checks sequence-length thresholds. That explains why flashattn2 is being chosen for seq=32/64.
Maya Chen: logs from runtime show attention kernel selection for a request: 
```
INFO kernel_select: model=gpt-small seq=64 hw=rtx-a100 selected_kernel=flashattn2 (heuristic_score=0.72)
INFO exec: attention_kernel=flashattn2 compile_flags="-O3 -march=sm80 -DENABLE_FLASHATTN"
```
Latency stack trace shows majority spent in kernel launch overhead + memcpy.
Ben Park: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back PR (abc123) 2) patch selector to reintroduce seq threshold 3) provide per-customer kernel override (env var) so we can flip acme to sdpa. Which do we want first?
Olivia Reyes: easiest short-term: set per-deployment override. We already have REDWOOD_KERNEL_ORDER env support but it was undocumented. You can set REDWOOD_KERNEL_ORDER=sdpa,flashattn2 for the dedicated pool or the customer route. Example: export REDWOOD_KERNEL_ORDER="sdpa,flashattn2" and restart runtime. That should pick sdpa for short sequences and restore p99.
Samir Patel: +1 for targeted override while we do a canary rollback to abc122 for the global change. I'll prepare a quick patch to kernel selector to re-add a min-seq check: if seq <= 128 then prefer sdpa. We'll also add a config knob REDWOOD_MIN_FLASHATTN_SEQ=128.
Maya Chen: can we do the override and a canary rollback in parallel? We need to communicate to the customer ASAP.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated — canary revert to commit abc122 (PR #3419) — started 04:55 UTC — target: canary then 100% after verification.
oncall-bot: assigned incident to oncall (L1): Ben Park — priority: P2 — please coordinate customer comms and postmortem.
Ben Park: I'm on it. I'll flip the per-customer kernel order for acme route now so they see improvement immediately while the rollback runs.
Olivia Reyes: test after override — I ran the same loadtest against acme's route with REDWOOD_KERNEL_ORDER=sdpa,flashattn2 and p99 dropped to ~320ms. Patch diff to show how to set per-route config: 
```
# per-route override example (console/api)
PATCH /v1/routes/acme-config
{
  "runtime_config": {
    "env": {
      "REDWOOD_KERNEL_ORDER": "sdpa,flashattn2"
    }
  }
}
```
Ben Park: done — config applied at 05:02 UTC. Customer reports latency back to normal. Will keep monitoring.
Samir Patel: root cause notes for postmortem: PR #3421 changed kernel priority without preserving historical seq thresholds. FlashAttn2's implementation has non-trivial kernel launch/dispatch overhead that amortizes only at seq >= ~128 on sm80-class GPUs with current compile flags. We should do one of the following: (a) make selector seq-aware, (b) add a compile-time/ run-time fast-path for short sequences in FlashAttn kernels, or (c) keep sdpa as default for seq<=128.
Olivia Reyes: add regression tests to CI that run short-seq synthetic workloads (seq 16/32/64/128) on the perf matrix and fail the PR if p99 regresses >20% relative to baseline. Also add a microbenchmark in buildkite to test kernel selection ordering.
Maya Chen: action items:
- Ben: coordinate customer comms (on it) + confirm no other routes impacted (05:10)
- Ben/Deploy: finish canary rollback to abc122 and monitor metrics (rollback in progress)
- Samir: patch kernel selector to reintroduce REDWOOD_MIN_FLASHATTN_SEQ and add config knob (PR target: today EOD)
- Olivia: add short-seq perf tests to CI and a quick repro script for SEs (PR target: tomorrow)
- Ops: add an automated alert when selector picks flashattn for seq < REDWOOD_MIN_FLASHATTN_SEQ
I'll draft a short incident summary for the customer and internal postmortem.
Ben Park: rollback to abc122 completed at 05:18 UTC — canary -> 100% after smoke checks. p99 across pool back to baseline. Closing escalation but keeping this thread open for follow-ups.
Maya Chen: thanks everyone. Follow-ups: include a perf note in PR review checklist about verifying short-seq overheads, and tag infra/research to prioritize a flashattn short-seq fast-path investigation.
Samir Patel: one extra: we should add a tiny unit test in the runtime that asserts kernel selection respects per-route override envs. I've opened a draft PR for the selector guard (draft-#3435).
Olivia Reyes: I'll upload the local repro logs and the loader script to the support ticket (ticket #SUP-5023) and attach the benchmark numbers.
Maya Chen: closing loop — customer notified and happy with mitigation. We'll do a formal postmortem after PRs land. Thanks all. :handshake:
